sections.sectionText: Topic: This course introduces students to natural fiber practices such as basketry, cordage-making, and introductory spinning and weaving, with an emphasis on foraging, preparing, and processing plant materials into usable fibers. The semester culminates in a collaborative project with the Red Oak Rain Garden, where students will design an outdoor escape-room experience that uses puzzles based on fiber arts and ecological knowledge. Some seats are reserved for A&D majors, A&D minors, and non-A&D majors. If you receive a "reserve closed" error, all seats for your major are filled, check back on December 1. sections.sectionText: Topic: Creative Catalysts: Making Art Inspired by Language, History, & Music Description: This course explores how language, history, music, and research can inspire innovative studio art practices. Through hands-on projects, students will engage with archival materials, linguistic structures, and historical narratives to develop a personalized, research-driven approach to creative work. Inspired by artists and thinkers like Arvo Pärt and Sophie Calle, the class emphasizes how stillness and “blank slate” thinking spark artistic transformation. Some seats are reserved for A&D majors, A&D minors, and non-A&D majors. If you receive a "reserve closed" error, all seats for your major are filled, check back on December 1. Any available seats left on December 1 will be made available to all majors. Graduate section.

sections.sectionText: Seminar: Methods Criticism, or “Practical Theory” is a graduate seminar that provides a selection of critical texts for engaging the ideas, contexts, and practices of contemporary art, with a significant part of the course content oriented toward the research interests of the participants. This course will emphasize strategies for addressing critical theory from a practical perspective: theory as a useful tool for understanding and articulating one’s creative research and practice.
